patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Campaign Monitor and MailerLite share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Campaign Monitor and MailerLite share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits. Choose Campaign Monitor only if your buying job matches “Design-led email marketing by Marigold with contact-tier Lite, Essentials, Premier, and En” rather than MailerLite's shape. Choose MailerLite only if your buying job matches “Simple email marketing for SMBs and creators with a free tier and approachable Comfort/Pow” rather than Campaign Monitor's shape. Workflow advantage: Campaign Monitor leans shared coverage; MailerLite leans ecommerce-email. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Campaign Monitor and MailerLite share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Campaign Monitor is Design-led email marketing by Marigold with contact-tier Lite, Essentials, Premier, and Enterprise.; MailerLite is Simple email marketing for SMBs and creators with a free tier and approachable Comfort/Power subscriber plans..
- Company-size focus: Campaign Monitor (small-business, mid-market) vs MailerLite (micro, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: Campaign Monitor-leaning — vs MailerLite-leaning ecommerce-email.
- Researched limits: Campaign Monitor — No forever free plan — trial only; MailerLite — Free caps at 250 subscribers / 2,500 emails per 30 days.

Limitations — Campaign Monitor: No forever free plan — trial only; Lite monthly send caps force upgrades for frequent senders; MailerLite: Free caps at 250 subscribers / 2,500 emails per 30 days; Automation and segmentation depth trail Klaviyo and ActiveCampaign.

Poor-fit cases: Campaign Monitor is a poor fit when that limitation bites: No forever free plan — trial only · MailerLite is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Free caps at 250 subscribers / 2,500 emails per 30 days · Avoid Campaign Monitor if you actually need MailerLite's motion (Simple email marketing for SMBs and creators with a free tier and approachable C)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
